rule: For each session, extract and store every explicit, atomic factual claim the user makes (named people, exact counts, purchases, specific venue or hostel names, job titles, trip plans, and direct preferences), attach the session date and a one-line source tag, and do not infer or generalize beyond the exact wording.
rationale: Many failures come from missing explicit facts (names, counts, purchases) or from the system failing to record them. Mapping every explicit atomic claim with its date/source ensures later stages can answer fact queries without inventing or omitting details. Prohibiting inference at map time prevents adding unsupported details that later appear as hallucinations.

rule: When the user expresses a preference or a memorable experience (e.g., likes 'live music' or 'enjoyed a bar encounter with Brandon Flowers'), record it as a concise preference/experience entry tied to the session date, but do not add related inferred hobbies, venues, or specifics unless the user explicitly stated them.
rationale: Failures show the pack either omits personal preferences or adds unsupported specifics. Capturing only explicit preferences/experiences preserves useful personalization while preventing the introduction of unsupported details.

rule: When merging entries about the same fact, keep the most recent explicit statement as authoritative for that fact, do not perform arithmetic or aggregations across dated counts unless the user explicitly recorded an aggregate, and mark any ambiguous or conflicting facts as 'conflict — multiple dated values' rather than choosing arbitrarily.
rationale: Incorrect numeric answers (off-by-one) and lost/contradicted facts arose from incorrect merging/aggregation. Using the latest explicit value prevents accidental overwriting with older data; forbidding implicit arithmetic and flagging conflicts prevents producing false confident answers.

rule: Whenever the user asserts a concrete personal fact (counts, purchases, place names, people and their roles, explicit preferences, or recommendations), create a discrete dated note that records the fact exactly as a short factual statement (subject, predicate, value) with the original session date and session id; include numeric values exactly and preserve proper names and titles verbatim.
rationale: Many failures come from missing explicit facts (counts, purchases, hostel name, advisor name) that were present earlier but not compiled into the memory pack. Capturing asserted facts verbatim, dated, and as structured short statements makes them retrievable and prevents later 'I don't know' answers when the information is actually present.

rule: If the user expresses a stable preference (e.g., travel preferences, venue types, dislikes) or a repeated personal interest, record it as a short dated preference note prefixed with 'pref:' and do not generalize or extrapolate beyond what was explicitly stated.
rationale: Failures include either missing preference data (hotel view/top amenities) or overly broad extrapolations. Explicit, labeled preference notes make it clear what may be used for personalization while avoiding unsupported assumptions.

rule: When merging notes about the same fact or entity, keep the most recent explicit factual statement as the canonical pack entry but also retain previous dated variants as provenance; never synthesize or infer undeclared details when conflicting or absent—if only older or ambiguous mentions exist, preserve them rather than inventing specifics.
rationale: Errors arose from missing or changed facts (counts, names) and from hallucinated inferences. Choosing the most recent explicit note as canonical while keeping provenance prevents loss of correct latest data and avoids inventing unsupported details.

rule: When the user states any concrete numeric, membership, or identity fact (counts, quantities, team composition numbers, explicit names or titles, purchases), create a dated discrete note that (a) records the exact value verbatim, (b) classifies the note with a type label such as 'count', 'identity', or 'purchase', and (c) marks an explicitness flag (explicit/implicit) so downstream stages can treat exact explicit statements as authoritative.
rationale: Many failures arise from numeric or identity facts being recorded but not classified or flagged as explicit, which makes them easy to omit or hedge when answering. Explicit type labels and an explicitness flag let the reduce stage identify authoritative facts (counts, names, purchases) and surface them directly.

rule: When merging notes, if there exists any most recent dated note flagged explicit for a given entity+type (e.g., a 'count' or 'identity' note), promote that note as the canonical pack entry and answer user queries about that fact directly and without hedging; keep older dated variants only as provenance. Separately, if there are two or more dated 'pref:' notes about the same topic that are consistent, synthesize a single stable preference entry summarizing them for use in recommendations.
rationale: Existing guidance to keep the most recent explicit statement is too vague in practice and led to either omission or hedged answers. This rule forces the reducer to produce and use a single canonical explicit fact (for counts/names/purchases) so answers are confident and accurate, and to consolidate repeated preference notes into a usable stable preference for suggestions.

rule: When the user reports or refers to a factual detail from an external source (an article, news item, recommendation, or other third-party content) as something they read, discussed, or want to remember, create a dated discrete note that records that fact verbatim and mark it explicit (include source label if provided, e.g., 'article', 'email', or URL).
rationale: Many failures came from facts the user mentioned only as 'in that article' or 'you recommended' (e.g., a named person in an article, a hostel name). Those are external facts the user treats as part of their memory context and should be captured as explicit dated notes so downstream merging can surface them.

rule: When the user affirms, confirms, accepts, or corrects a specific factual statement (including counts, diagnoses, purchases, or a previously suggested recommendation), create or update a dated discrete note recording the confirmed fact verbatim and mark it explicit; if this confirms or corrects an earlier note, link the new note to the prior note id for provenance.
rationale: Failures show the system missed facts users explicitly confirmed (counts, purchases, health issue, recommendation acceptance). Recording confirmations as explicit updates ensures the most recent user-affirmed value will be promoted by reduce-stage logic.
